description: Hosts one child in a native WPF viewport with independently configurable horizontal and vertical scrolling. Place it in a bounded parent such as a fixed or star-sized Grid row or column; a StackPanel in the scrolling axis expands instead of creating a viewport. For a deliberate partial continuation, keep every repeated child full-size and expose enough of the next surface to remain recognizable, normally about one quarter to one half. Keep readable text and actions in the safe region. When edge navigation is required, reserve a trailing gutter at least as wide as the compact control footprint, then overlay the control in the same Grid cell without obscuring media or text; do not fake continuation with a narrow final child or detached label.

horizontalScrollBarVisibility.description: Horizontal scrolling policy. Auto exposes native scrollbar chrome when content exceeds the viewport; for a polished media rail, use Hidden only when another browse affordance explains the scroll interaction.

verticalScrollBarVisibility.description: Vertical scrolling policy. Auto exposes native scrollbar chrome when content exceeds the viewport; Hidden keeps scrolling available without visible chrome.

canContentScroll.description: Use logical item scrolling when the hosted content supports IScrollInfo; false keeps pixel-based scrolling for arbitrary layouts.

padding.description: Inner WPF Thickness between the viewport edge and its content.

margin.description: Outer WPF Thickness separating the viewport from adjacent layout.

content.description: Single layout or control subtree hosted by the scrollable viewport.
